skill.name: brainstorming
skill.description: Guide collaborative discovery before implementation by clarifying goals, comparing approaches, and validating architecture, data flow, error handling, and testing decisions.
skill.summary: Turn early ideas into validated technical designs through focused questions and structured trade-off analysis.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Early feature ideas often hide unclear goals, constraints, and technical risks. This skill guides focused discovery, approach comparison, and incremental design validation before implementation.
actual_capabilities: Reviews available project files, documentation, and recent commits to understand the current context.
Asks one focused question per message to clarify purpose, constraints, and success criteria.
Presents two or three approaches with trade-offs, a recommendation, and supporting reasoning.
Develops designs in reviewable sections covering architecture, components, data flow, error handling, and testing.
Records an approved design and prepares a structured handoff for implementation planning.
limitations: Requires interactive answers and may need several rounds before producing a complete design.
Depends on accurate project context and cannot verify unstated business or user assumptions.
Does not replace security review, user research, implementation testing, or expert architectural approval.
May write and commit design documents, so repository actions require careful review.

use_cases.title: Define a New Feature
use_cases.description: Clarify requirements, constraints, and acceptance criteria before changing an existing application.

use_cases.title: Scope a Product Idea
use_cases.description: Convert a broad request into comparable options and a reviewable technical direction.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Architecture Choices
use_cases.description: Compare designs across data flow, failure handling, testing, and delivery complexity.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a Feature Idea
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me refine [idea] for [users]. Ask one question at a time, then summarize the goal, constraints, and success criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when an idea is clear enough to discuss but lacks detailed requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Implementation Approaches
prompt_templates.prompt: Explore two or three approaches for [feature]. Explain trade-offs, recommend one option, and identify the decisions needed before implementation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the desired outcome is known but the technical direction is uncertain.

prompt_templates.title: Develop a Technical Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Design [system change] in sections. Cover architecture, components, data flow, error handling, and testing. Pause after each section for validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when requirements are stable and stakeholders need an incremental design review.

prompt_templates.title: Challenge an Advanced Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review project context for [initiative]. Challenge assumptions, compare three architectures, and identify operational, migration, security, and testing risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before a complex or high-impact implementation begins.

output_examples.input: I want to add team invitations.
output: Goal: Let administrators invite members with clear expiration and access rules.
Open question: Should invitations expire automatically after seven days?
Next step: Confirm roles and resend behavior before selecting an implementation.

output_examples.input: Compare notification delivery approaches for our application.
output: Recommended: Use queued delivery for retry control and predictable request latency.
Alternative: Send synchronously for simpler operations, with slower requests and weaker failure recovery.
Decision needed: Confirm delivery volume, acceptable delay, and duplicate handling.

output_examples.input: Design a staged migration from local accounts to single sign-on.
output: Architecture: Add federated login beside existing authentication during a controlled transition.
Data flow: Link verified identities to existing accounts before enabling federated access.
Risk review: Test rollback, account recovery, duplicate identities, and partial provider outages.

best_practices: Provide the current project context, target users, constraints, and measurable success criteria.
Answer each discovery question before requesting a final design.
Review every design section and correct assumptions before continuing.
anti_patterns: Do not request implementation before goals and constraints are understood.
Do not choose an approach without comparing meaningful alternatives.
Do not approve repository writes or commits without reviewing the design.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it before implementing a feature, component, behavior change, or architecture decision.

faq.question: Does it write implementation code?
faq.answer: No. Its primary output is a validated design and an optional handoff to implementation planning.

faq.question: Why does it ask one question at a time?
faq.answer: Focused questions reduce cognitive load and allow each answer to guide the next decision.

faq.question: What project access does it need?
faq.answer: It benefits from access to relevant files, documentation, and recent commits.

faq.question: Can it compare several technical options?
faq.answer: Yes. It presents two or three approaches, explains trade-offs, and recommends one with reasoning.

faq.question: Will it change my repository?
faq.answer: The workflow may write and commit a design document. Review and approve repository actions before they occur.
